importance_ranking.reason: Control pulpits vary significantly in form — open platform vs fully enclosed AC cabin vs crane-mounted cab — and buyers must visually confirm the structural type, glazing configuration, and mounting arrangement before any other evaluation. Wrong type = immediate skip; no text description substitutes for a photo of the actual fabricated unit.

Buyers shortlist on enclosure type, material, dimensions, and environmental features (AC, acoustic insulation, heat-resistant glass) — these are non-interchangeable requirements driven by plant layout and operating conditions. A listing without specs cannot be evaluated for project fit.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in this category; buyers search by fabrication capability, material quality, and project references rather than by manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: EPC contractors and plant operators evaluate fabricator credentials — structural engineering capability, past project references in steel/power plants, ISO certification, and delivery track record — before committing to a custom-fabricated capital item. Seller identity is a qualification gate, not a brand preference.

Every control pulpit is custom-dimensioned and project-quoted; no standard list price exists. Displayed price serves only as a budget entry point for initial feasibility screening — final price is always negotiated after scope confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: All variants — open platform, enclosed cabin, crane-mounted cab — are supplied and quoted per complete unit. No buyer questions this; unit ambiguity does not arise in this category.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied: a control pulpit is always sold as one complete fabricated structure. Showing 'per piece' adds no information and project-based pricing means there is no per-unit price to qualify.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Material (Steel vs FRP vs Wood) defines the structural class of the pulpit — non-interchangeable across plant environments, with steel being mandatory for steel mills and heavy industrial use while FRP suits corrosive or lighter-duty applications, driving significant price and fabrication cost differences.

Built Type (Prefab vs Panel Build vs Modular) determines the construction method and site installation complexity — modular units allow phased assembly in constrained spaces while prefab units are delivered complete, directly affecting project logistics cost and lead time.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Whether the pulpit is open-type (platform with railings), closed with fan ventilation, or fully AC-enclosed is the primary buyer shortlisting criterion — it determines thermal comfort, noise protection, and suitability for the operating environment.

Fixed/stationary ground-mounted, elevated platform-mounted, and crane-cab-mounted (travels with crane bridge) are non-interchangeable configurations that determine structural design, civil interface requirements, and applicable safety standards.

Toughened glass, laminated safety glass, and heat-resistant glass for steel mill environments are distinct safety and compliance requirements — buyers in steel plants and foundries mandate specific glazing standards that sellers must confirm upfront.
